question.problem:
Consider the triangle $C$ in the plane with vertices $(0,0),(1,1)$ and $(0,1),$ and the region $D$ bounded by $C.$ According to Green's theorem, 

$$
{∮}_{C}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y\,dx+(xy+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡y)\,dy={∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

Calculate the function $f(x,y).$
question.worked_solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing $D$, then Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dx+Q\,dy={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14223852/assets/5673a3eadfa3c01dbb9e2c8bf497b17f34a834d950621afa7d480af625ce1e18.png)

We have that $P(x,y)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y$ and $Q(x,y)=xy+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡y.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂y}=-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡y,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂x}=y-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡y.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y\,dx+(xy+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡y)\,dy & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}[y-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡y-(-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡y)]\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(y-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡y+\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}y\,\text{d}A\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $f(x,y)=y.$
